feed.title: Hamon Lab
feed.subtitle: The Hamon Lab investigates how macrophage diversity shapes cancer progression, immune responses, and treatment outcomes. By combining human samples, spatial technologies, and experimental models, we aim to uncover new strategies to harness macrophage biology for cancer therapy.

entry.title: A new milestone for the lab!

link.title: A new milestone for the lab!

entry.content:
Camille Da Silva has been awarded a PhD fellowship and will continue her research on macrophages in liver cancer as the lab’s first PhD student.

Congratulations to Camille Da Silva on being awarded a PhD fellowship!

After joining the Macrophages & Cancer team as a Master’s student, Camille will continue her research with us as our first PhD student.

Her PhD project will focus on understanding the role of macrophages in liver cancer, with a particular interest in how macrophage diversity and function influence tumor progression and response to therapy.

This fellowship marks an important milestone for Camille and for our young team. Congratulations again, Camille!

View the original post on LinkedIn
